extracted.intended_audience: research funders, NLP/text-mining researchers, scientometrics researchers, grant administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Using supervised NLP / machine learning to identify content categories in grant peer review reports, based on human-annotated corpora and fine-tuned transformer models to enable large-scale, structured analysis for funders and researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twelve content categories for grant peer review reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Developed twelve categories reflecting content of grant peer review reports that are of interest to research funders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories form the target labels for annotation and automatic classification. They were created as the basis for an annotated corpus of Swiss National Science Foundation review reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative multi-annotator annotation process
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple human annotators iteratively annotated the twelve categories in a novel text corpus of grant peer review reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotation should be performed by multiple annotators with iterations to refine category definitions and improve consistency; human annotation must be validated before use for model training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human annotation validation / reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate that categories can be reliably identified by human annotators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only categories with satisfactory human annotation reliability should be used as targets; perceived annotator difficulty correlates with model performance and should inform category selection or redefinition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fine-tune pre-trained transformer models for classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Use annotated texts to fine-tune pre-trained transformer models to classify the defined categories at scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model fine-tuning on the validated annotated corpus is the primary automated approach; architectures and pre-trained checkpoints chosen will affect downstream performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of classification approach affects performance
rubrics_metrics.description: The choice of text classification approach considerably influences the classification performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare multiple classification methods and report differences; selection should be based on empirical performance, robustness, and suitability for each category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness and validation checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct several robustness and validation checks on the machine learning models and their predictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include out-of-sample evaluation and other validation procedures. The paper reports a high correspondence between out-of-sample classification performance and human annotators' perceived difficulty, indicating these checks are essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scalability to enable structured reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Models should enable classification of categories at scale to allow researchers and funders to examine and report on report contents in a structured manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize scalable pipelines so large corpora of peer review reports can be analyzed efficiently; provide and share fine-tuned models to facilitate reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal: contribute to quality and trustworthiness of grant peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: The overall aim is that this approach can contribute to ensuring the quality and trustworthiness of grant peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use outputs to inform funders and stakeholders about content patterns in reviews; present results transparently and consider limitations of automated classification when drawing conclusions.
